The thin uv-tool CLI is a client of /api/users and writes no user files, but
it can't import the backend, so it carries its own UserManifest
(mycelium-cli/src/mycelium/protocol.py) and normalizes a handle and its team
slugs before sending them. That normalization has to match the backend's or
the handle the CLI shows is not the one keying the record it just wrote — so
the CLI suite locks the `normalize` fixture and the wire fields, and the
backend suite locks all of it.
If a change to the shared shape is genuinely intended, update this file in
the same change and both suites re-lock to the new value.
